sources.locator: United States, July 1, 2020 to July 1, 2025

assumptions.citation: Middle: Mayer and Somerville (2000), p. 651: a 1 percent increase in house prices results in a temporary 15 percent increase in new construction over six quarters; read as 15% of one quarter's construction spread over 20 quarters, 0.15 / 20 = 0.75% of 5 years' construction. Low: the same paper, p. 653, finds the impact fee coefficient not statistically different from zero. High: Baum-Snow and Han (2024) housing unit supply elasticity 0.3, half assumed to arrive within 5 years, divided by U.S. housing unit growth of 5.29% from July 2020 to July 2025: 0.3 x 0.5 / 0.0529 = 2.84. What the team re-read (decision 67): the 5.29% growth, 148,260,882 / 140,817,690 - 1 = 0.0529 (United States row of the Census county housing-unit file CO-EST2025-HU.xlsx, July 1 2020 and 2025, re-read 2026-11-03); Albouy et al.'s demand elasticity and the Census new-home prices used beside this entry. Carried from Adam Ruege's v2.0 record and not yet re-read: the Mayer and Somerville quotes on pp. 651 and 653 (paywalled) and Baum-Snow and Han's 0.3 (the publisher returned HTTP 403 and no open abstract was found on 2026-11-03).
assumptions.rationale: No study measures a cut near $25,000 per unit; the range runs from no response to a long-run supply response.
assumptions.transferability: National; no state-specific estimate exists.

record.law: RSA 674:71 to 674:73, as amended by H.B. 577 (2025, chapter 197) and H.B. 1079 (2026, chapter 210); first enacted by S.B. 146 (2016, chapter 6)
record.summary: Every New Hampshire town or city with zoning must allow one attached or detached ADU by right in every district that allows single-family homes, and may require the owner to live in one of the two units.
record.quote: One accessory dwelling unit, which may be either attached or detached, shall be allowed as a matter of right.
record.in_effect: 2025 changes effective July 1, 2025; 2026 chapter 210 effective August 31, 2026 (ADUs required in some form since June 1, 2017)

features.challenge_requirement: Allow one ADU on a parcel with an existing single-family building.
features.observed_position: The section requires one attached or detached ADU as of right on covered single-family lots, subject to specified exceptions.

sources.title: New Hampshire RSA 674:72
sources.locator: paragraph I
sources.quote: One accessory dwelling unit, which may be either attached or detached

limitations: Municipal owner-occupancy (paragraph VI), dimensional, utility and other permitted conditions remain.
The number of affected parcels has not been measured.

features.observed_position: The current text expressly includes attached or detached ADUs.

sources.title: New Hampshire RSA 674:72
sources.locator: paragraph I

limitations: Municipal dimensional and utility conditions remain.

features.challenge_requirement: Allow ADUs of at least 600 square feet.
features.observed_position: Municipalities may not set the maximum below 750 square feet; the general cap is 950 unless the municipality allows more. This supports 600 on covered sites.

sources.title: New Hampshire RSA 674:72
sources.locator: paragraph VII
sources.quote: may not restrict the total living space to less than 750 square feet

features.challenge_requirement: Require no added parking for the ADU.
features.observed_position: A municipality may require one additional space, so the statute does not supply the challenge zero-parking rule.

sources.title: New Hampshire RSA 674:72
sources.locator: paragraph IV
sources.quote: it may require up to one additional parking space for each accessory dwelling unit

limitations: Whether towns use the option has not been surveyed.

adu.strength_rationale: Starting rule (decision 62): three of the four benchmark features (one ADU per lot, attached or detached, at least 600 square feet) are supported with limits and one (no added parking) differs, so 3 / 4 = 0.75 of the benchmark is already in law and 0.25 is newly affected. Owner-occupancy may still be required (paragraph VI); human review pending.

current_law_default: States and scenarios with no file default to current strength 0: "No statewide law found; local permissions unverified."
